## Revenue grew 10% on steady volume
layout: section
kicker: Results

## Revenue beat last year in each month of Q3
layout: chart
kicker: Results
subtitle: Monthly revenue, $ thousands
takeaway: Q3 revenue reached $2.77M, up 10% on the third quarter of 2025

```chart
type: line
number_format: '$#,##0'
labels: false
categories: [Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep]
series:
  - name: "2026"
    values: [812, 798, 845, 860, 872, 851, 905, 918, 942]
  - name: "2025"
    values: [790, 776, 801, 812, 820, 806, 829, 838, 851]
```

Notes:
September was the best month on record, helped by the school term start.
Source: general ledger, revenue by month, January to September of 2025 and 2026.

## North, east and online grew 14% or more
layout: table
kicker: Results
subtitle: Revenue by region, third quarter
takeaway: Government is the only region that shrank, after one contract ended

| Region | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 | Change | Accounts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| North | $742K | $846K | +14% | 42 |
| South | $611K | $648K | +6% | 38 |
| East | $498K | $571K | +15% | 27 |
| West | $402K | $419K | +4% | 31 |
| Online | $188K | $214K | +14% | 210 |
| Government | $77K | $67K | -13% | 6 |

Notes:
The government drop is the county library contract, which moved to a framework supplier in July.
Source: general ledger, revenue by region; account counts from the CRM on September 30.

## Volume held steady as recycled took share
layout: chart
kicker: Results
subtitle: Cases shipped by product line, thousands
takeaway: Recycled grew from 21% to 28% of volume in a year

```chart
type: stacked-column
number_format: '0.0'
labels: true
categories: [Q4 2025, Q1 2026, Q2 2026, Q3 2026]
series:
  - name: Copy paper
    values: [41.2, 40.1, 39.0, 37.8]
  - name: Recycled
    values: [12.4, 13.9, 15.6, 17.3]
  - name: Card and specialty
    values: [6.1, 6.0, 6.3, 6.2]
```

Notes:
Total volume rose 3% over the four quarters while copy paper fell 8%.
Source: warehouse shipment ledger, cases shipped by product line, October 2025 to September 2026.

## Offices brought in nearly half of revenue
layout: chart
kicker: Results
subtitle: Share of Q3 revenue by customer segment
takeaway: Schools and hospitals now make up 36% of revenue

```chart
type: bar
number_format: '0%'
labels: true
categories: [Offices, Schools, Hospitals, Retail, Online]
series:
  - name: Share of revenue
    values: [0.48, 0.22, 0.14, 0.09, 0.07]
```

Notes:
Schools are 22% and hospitals 14%; schools rose from 19% a year ago on the two district contracts. Retail is 9% and online 7%.
Source: general ledger revenue joined to CRM segment codes, third quarter of 2026.

## Margin and service: where we lost ground
layout: section
kicker: Customers and operations

## Freight pushed three lines' margins down
layout: chart
kicker: Customers and operations
subtitle: Change in gross margin, Q3 2026 against Q3 2025, points
takeaway: Copy paper and packaging wrap lost the most, both heavy to ship

```chart
type: bar
number_format: '+0.0;-0.0;0.0'
labels: true
legend: false
categories: [Copy paper, Recycled, Card stock, Envelopes, Specialty, Packaging wrap]
series:
  - name: Margin change, points
    values: [-1.8, 2.4, 0.6, -0.9, 1.2, -2.6]
```

Notes:
Diesel surcharges added about $31K to freight cost in the quarter. Recycled gained on the new mill price.
Source: product margin report from finance, third quarter of 2025 and 2026.

## On-time delivery recovered in September
layout: table
kicker: Customers and operations
takeaway: The second north shift cut late orders by half from July to September

| Month | Orders | On time | Late | Back orders |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| July | 4,812 | 94.1% | 284 | 37 |
| August | 4,955 | 95.3% | 233 | 22 |
| September | 5,104 | 97.2% | 143 | 9 |

Notes:
The second shift started on August 4. Back orders fell as the main mill caught up.
Source: dispatch system delivery log, July to September 2026.

## Evening routes worked; web orders did not
layout: two-col
kicker: Customers and operations
takeaway: The web form fix comes first in Q4

### left
- A second north shift halved late orders
- Evening routes added 31 same-day accounts
- Volume pricing tiers kept office buyers

### right
- The web form dropped lines on timeouts
- Online repeat orders fell 4% in August
- The fix slipped to the October release

Notes:
Left is what moved the quarter; right is what held it back.
Source: dispatch system delivery log for late orders and routes; web analytics for online repeat orders.

## Three risks could cost us Q4 margin
layout: bands-3
kicker: Customers and operations
label1: Freight costs
label2: Supplier capacity
label3: The county contract

### text1
- Diesel surcharges rose **6%** in September
- Two carriers asked to reprice in January

### text2
- Our main mill runs at **94%** of capacity
- A second mill is qualified as a backup

### text3
- The county contract ends in December
- **$67K** of Q3 revenue rides on the rebid

Notes:
Source: carrier invoices for surcharges, the mill's capacity letter of September 12, and the regional revenue table earlier in this section.
